description: Banana anthracnose is a major fungal disease affecting banana fruits both before and after harvest. It is mainly caused by the fungus Colletotrichum musae. The disease produces sunken dark lesions on fruits that expand during ripening and can cause serious postharvest losses during storage and transport.
affected_parts: Leaves and shoots in severe infections
symptoms: Dark sunken lesions on banana fruit surface
Lesions enlarge and become black or dark brown during ripening
Orange spore masses (acervuli) appear on mature lesions
Leaf blight and shoot dieback in severe cases
Premature leaf drop and reduced yield
disease_cycle: Fungus infects immature banana fruits in the field
Spores germinate and form appressoria to penetrate plant tissue
Infection remains latent (quiescent stage) in immature fruits
Symptoms develop when fruits ripen after harvest
Spores spread through rain splash, wind, tools and infected plant material
field_and_postharvest_damage: Crown rot in harvested banana clusters
Reduced fruit quality and market value
chemical_control: Carbendazim 12% + Mancozeb 63% WP (Samartha): 300–400 g per acre
Thiophanate Methyl 70% WP (KTM): 250–600 g per acre
Mancozeb 75% WP (K ZEB): 500 g per acre
All in One fungicide: 1.5–2 g per liter
biological_control: Use of biological antagonists such as Trichoderma species
Natural plant extracts and microbial biocontrol agents
Integrated disease management strategies combining biological agents and cultural practices
cultural_management: Maintain good plantation hygiene and remove infected plant debris
Ensure good air circulation in banana plantations
Harvest fruits carefully to avoid wounds
prevention: Select resistant banana varieties where available
Monitor fruit during pre-harvest and postharvest stages
Maintain clean storage and transport conditions
sources: Plant pathology research on Colletotrichum musae
Agricultural extension publications on banana diseases
